result.summary: This PR fixes the first-run disk-space warning shown by bitcoind/bitcoin-qt on startup: it relabels the assumed blockchain size as GiB instead of the incorrect GB, and for pruned nodes it now displays the same rounded byte estimate that CheckDiskSpace actually uses rather than the full-chain estimate. It also corrects the doc comments in kernel/chainparams.h describing the assumed sizes' units. This revives a fix originally attempted in #29678.
result.problem: Users setting up a node for the first time see a disk-space warning that mislabels units (GB vs GiB) and, when pruning, shows a full-chain estimate unrelated to the actual (lower) prune-based check, which can misinform storage planning. A reviewer (mercie-ux) traced a real 63 GB gap between what the check required and what was displayed.

open_concerns: hebasto notes an inconsistency: -prune has MiB granularity but the warning now shows a GiB-rounded figure, which can look odd for small prune targets (e.g. -prune=550 showing '1 GiB')
fanquake raised that changing displayed strings post-freeze may block merge timing, unrelated to code correctness

result.card: This PR fixes the first-run disk-space warning in bitcoind/bitcoin-qt to correctly label sizes as GiB and to show the same (pruned-aware) estimate that the underlying disk-space check uses, rather than a mismatched full-chain figure. It revives a fix from the closed #29678 and touches only src/init.cpp and a doc comment in kernel/chainparams.h. Reviewer mercie-ux confirmed a real 63 GB discrepancy between the old warning and the actual check, and jeanpablojp verified correct pruned-case behavior; achow101 and murchandamus gave ACKs. hebasto raised an unresolved, nonblocking concern that -prune's MiB granularity can look odd next to a GiB-rounded warning, and fanquake noted the change may be affected by the project's string/translation freeze. The PR is small, self-contained, and currently reviewable, with no dependency blocking it.
